subject.title: MEDIA: directive with absolute local paths outside default media roots silently fails (Telegram)

question: Should this issue be limited to better diagnostics for blocked Telegram reply `MEDIA:` paths while root expansion stays with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 or the `tools.fs.roots` design, or should it define a new root-access policy itself?
rationale: The source-backed failure is real, but allowing more absolute host-local paths changes the model-facing file-read/upload boundary and cannot be safely selected by automation.

options.title: Diagnostics here, root policy elsewhere
options.body: Keep this issue focused on warn-level reasoned logs and optional safe in-message unavailable notices, while configurable roots remain in the broader security-reviewed root-policy items.

options.title: Define root policy here
options.body: Use this issue as the canonical Telegram outbound root-expansion contract and require schema, docs, upgrade, security, and live Telegram proof before implementation.

options.title: Close as current policy
options.body: Treat out-of-root host paths as intentionally blocked and only require users to use managed roots, explicit read-enabled policy, or `openclaw message send --media`.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics here, root policy elsewhere
recommendation.body: Keep this issue focused on warn-level reasoned logs and optional safe in-message unavailable notices, while configurable roots remain in the broader security-reviewed root-policy items.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history on outbound media access and the host-read boundary used by this reply media path.
